title: The Vending Machine
logline: The basement vending machine keeps giving Priya more than she paid for.

cast.name: Priya
cast.description: early-30s night-shift data clerk, worn out, careful

cast.name: The Machine
cast.description: an old glass-front snack vending machine, humming, one buzzing tube light above it
visual_tags: handwritten OUT OF ORDER tag on coil A4

panels.scene: Wide low-angle shot of a concrete office basement at night. Priya stands small before a glowing vending machine, the only light source, her long shadow stretching back toward the stairs.
panels.narration: Every night at 2 a.m. I go down for a coffee. Every night the machine gives me one extra thing.

panels.scene: Close on the dispensing tray. Two items sit in it: a can of coffee and a second can turned so a small taped paper note faces out. Priya's hand with chipped red polish reaches in.
Priya under the buzzing tube light holding the note up to read it. Her face is lit hard from below. The note is small, handwritten, its words not legible to us.
panels.narration: The first note said 'you left your window open.' It was right.

panels.scene: A row of the previous nights' notes laid out on Priya's tidy desk beside her keyboard, each taped to a can. She stands over them, arms crossed, cardigan pulled tight.
panels.narration: By night six they weren't about my apartment anymore. They were about the basement. About tonight.

panels.scene: Priya crouched at the dispensing tray again. In it is a single glossy photograph, no can. The tube light above her flickers, half the frame dropping into black.
Extreme close on the photo in her trembling hand: a grainy shot of Priya asleep in her own bed, taken from above. Her waking eyes are reflected in the photo's glossy surface, wide.
panels.narration: The photo was timestamped 2:14 a.m. My watch said 2:11.

caption:
Every night the basement vending machine gives her one extra thing. Night seven, it gave her a photo. 😨

Would you keep going back down there? Follow for a new comic every few days.
